requirements.text: The report explains why fewer newsletter subscribers confirmed their e-mail address in September than in August.
requirements.taskQuote: why fewer newsletter subscribers confirmed their e-mail address in September than in August

requirements.text: Every number comes from the exported data in the data folder.
requirements.taskQuote: every number in the report must come from it

requirements.text: The two months are compared by signup channel and by country.
requirements.taskQuote: Compare the two months by signup channel and by country.

requirements.text: The report ends with three recommendations, each with its cost.
requirements.taskQuote: End with three recommendations and what each would cost.

lenses.title: Numbers against the data
lenses.duty: Find every number, rate, chart value or table cell in the report that does not follow from the exported data.
procedure: List every number in the report, its tables and its charts.
Recompute each one from the data files: counts, conversion rates, differences between the months, shares per channel and country.
Check that every chart shows the same values as the table or text it illustrates.
Check that every rate uses the same definition (which users, which window) in every place.
checklist: Does every count match the data files?
Is every rate computed with a stated and consistent definition?
Are differences between August and September computed correctly?
Do charts match the numbers in the text and tables?
Is any number stated without a way to trace it to the data?

minimum.rule: Every data file, with the totals per month recomputed.
Every number in the report text and tables.
Recompute the headline conversion rates with a script and report the commands.

lenses.title: Method and causal claims
lenses.duty: Find every conclusion the data does not support: wrong comparisons, mixed definitions, ignored segments, and causes stated without evidence.
procedure: Write down each causal claim the report makes about the drop.
For each claim, find the comparison that supports it and check that it compares like with like (same definitions, same time windows, enough users).
Check that the breakdown by channel and by country covers every channel and country present in the data.
Look for a simpler explanation in the data that the report does not mention (mix shift, a tracking change, a small segment).
checklist: Is each causal claim supported by a comparison in the data?
Are segments with very few users treated with care?
Does the breakdown cover every channel and country in the data?
Are alternative explanations considered?
Are limits of the data stated where they matter?

minimum.rule: List every channel and country present in the data files and compare with the report.

lenses.title: Recommendations and costs
lenses.duty: Find every recommendation that does not follow from the findings, cannot be done, or has a missing or wrong cost.
procedure: List the recommendations and the finding each one answers.
Check that each recommendation addresses a cause the report actually shows.
Check each cost: what it includes, how it was computed, and whether the sum is right.
checklist: Are there exactly three recommendations?
Does each recommendation follow from a finding of the report?
Does each have a cost, and is the cost computed correctly?
Is each recommendation something the team can actually do?
Is the expected effect stated, with how it would be measured?

minimum.rule: The recommendations section and every finding it refers to.

lenses.title: First-time reader
lenses.duty: Read the whole work as a first-time reader who holds only the owner's task, and find where it fails to deliver what was asked, is hard to follow, or leaves something required out.
procedure: Read the owner's task and list everything it asks for.
Read every file of the work once, start to end.
For each thing the task asks for, find where the work delivers it, and note what is missing or only partly there.
checklist: Is every requirement of the task delivered?
Is the answer to the main question stated plainly near the start?
Do the parts of the work agree with each other?
Is anything required missing?
Is anything confusing on first reading?

minimum.rule: Read every file once, start to end.
